`emit_epilogue_impl` (riscv/prologue.rs:101) and `emit_epilogue_and_ret_impl` (riscv/prologue.rs:548) are the same seven lines in the same impl: clone `used_callee_saved`, restore each with `-frame_size + i*8` through `emit_load_from_s0(.., "ld")`, then `emit_epilogue_riscv(frame_size)`; the second only appends `emit("    ret")`. The second can call the first, and the x86 member at x86/prologue.rs:167 repeats the same restore loop with `phys_reg_name`.

Read emit_inline_asm at 1286 to 1291 beside emit_inline_asm_with_segs at 1293 to 1297 in src/backend/x86/codegen/emit.rs: each is a three-statement delegation that forwards to a common inline-asm routine, emits callee-saved clobber annotations and invalidates the register cache. The second calls a different callee with an extra seg_overrides argument, so the entire difference lives in the delegated name and nothing is left to factor.

`f64_to_f128_bytes_lossless` (long_double.rs:1028) and `f64_to_x87_bytes_simple` (long_double.rs:1143) share only a three-line guard: `f64_decompose`, a zero return and an inf/NaN dispatch, and even there the difference is which format's constructors are named (`make_f128_zero/infinity/nan` versus `make_x87_zero/infinity/nan`). The normal paths are the two distinct encodings themselves, an implicit-bit binary128 packed by hand versus an explicit-integer-bit x87 word handed to `x87_encode`, so the pair mirrors two formats by design and factoring the guard would need a constructor triple passed in to save six lines.

The pair is f128_bytes_to_u64 (1106) and f128_bytes_to_u128 (1132), each a five-line delegation: call f128_to_abs_uint(bytes, 64|128)?, and if the sign bit is set hand off to the signed sibling f128_bytes_to_i64 / f128_bytes_to_i128 and cast, otherwise cast abs_val. The whole difference is the width literal, the sibling called and the target type, so factoring means a macro or a numeric-trait generic wrapping five lines of body, twice. That costs more than it saves on two public, separately documented conversion entry points whose per-width spelling is the readable form.

Read lower_builtin_isnan at 221 to 236 beside lower_builtin_isfinite at 255 to 270 in src/ir/lowering/expr_builtins_fpclass.rs: the empty-args guard, lower_fp_classify_arg, the whole F128 libcall and classify_result_to_bool branch, and the bitcast plus fp_masks prologue are repeated verbatim, with only the final mask and comparison differing. That prologue is a scaffold one helper taking the libcall name would serve for all four builtins.

expand_urem32_in_i64 (1596) and expand_srem32_in_i64 (1630) both spell out the same x % C = x - (x / C) * C lowering: fresh quotient from a div expander, a Mul into a fresh prod, then a Sub into dest, differing only in which div helper is called, in d's signedness and in the power-of-two guard. The same scaffold is written six times in this file (expand_urem32 at 773, expand_srem32 at 819, expand_urem64 at 1231, expand_srem64 at 1266), so one helper taking the quotient expander and the constant would serve all of them without changing behavior.

put_piece_no_hash (172) and remove_piece_no_hash (181) are four statements each on the same bitboard triple: bb = 1u64 << sq, then pieces[pt] and colors[color] combined with the bitboard, then mailbox[sq] set. They differ in the operator (|= against ^=) and in the mailbox value (pt against NO_PIECE_TYPE), which is the mirror-image pair a chess board representation is written as by design. Both are #[inline] and sit on the make/unmake hot path, so a merged version taking an operator or direction flag adds a branch or a closure to save three lines.

Read bishop_attacks_setwise_avx2 beside rook_attacks_setwise_avx2 in src/setwise.rs: both splat bb, mask the empty squares with notwrap, run kogge_stone_fill, shift4 and fold4_or in the same six statements, differing only in the four direction constants and which lanes carry a file mask. One macro or a const generic wrapper would emit both bodies unchanged.

wrap_c (254) and wrap_cpp (316) repeat roughly forty lines verbatim: the same `int main`/`void main` early return, the same functions/body/in_fn/brace_depth state machine counting '{' and '}' per trimmed line with the same saturating_sub, the same single-line-function special case, and the same emit loop indenting each body line by four spaces before `return 0;`. Only three things vary: the regex (C_FN_PATTERN against CPP_FN_PATTERN), the include list, and the extra `using namespace std;`. One function taking the pattern and a prelude string serves both with no behavior change, and the brace-counting heuristic is exactly the code you do not want maintained in two copies.

load_sqlite (80) and load_duckdb (109) are the per-engine TPC-C loaders of a benchmark harness: they mirror each other by design so the same workload is replayed on rusqlite and duckdb, behind separate feature gates, over unrelated concrete connection types and diverging APIs (conn.execute("ANALYZE", []) versus conn.execute_batch("ANALYZE")), each calling its own create_tpcc_schema_* and load_*_sqlite/duckdb family. Factoring would mean inventing a trait over three third-party drivers, which is exactly the benchmark comparison pair the rule's scope excludes.

Read load_item_sqlite at 903 to 919 beside load_item_duckdb at 1258 to 1274 in crates/vibesql-bench-common/src/tpcc/schema.rs: the same TPC-C item loading loop, differing only in the connection type and the driver params macro, each gated behind its own cargo feature. This is one benchmark loader replayed under a second engine harness, which is what the file exists to do.

The pair is create_assertion (assertions.rs:7) and create_domain (domains.rs:11), each a four-to-six line insert-if-absent over a different map field, a different value type and a different CatalogError variant; create_domain additionally lowercases the key and rewrites the stored name, so the bodies are not even behaviorally identical. The whole remaining difference lives in the erased names, and unifying it would need a generic map-plus-error-constructor helper larger than the lines it saves.

Read create_role at 90 to 97 in crates/vibesql-catalog/src/store/privileges.rs beside create_schema at 8 to 15 in crates/vibesql-catalog/src/store/schemas.rs: both are the four-line contains-then-insert idiom, but one guards a role set and the other a schema map keyed by name with its own error variant and a constructed Schema value. The shared body is short and its whole difference is the erased names and types.

apply_in_subquery_affinity_coercion exists twice under the same name and signature, at in_subquery.rs:1047 and expressions/subqueries.rs:860; diffing the two windows leaves only the import spelling (Option<TypeAffinity> against Option<vibesql_types::TypeAffinity>, `use vibesql_types::SqlValue` against `use vibesql_types::{SqlValue, TypeAffinity}`) and one extra doc line. Roughly sixty lines of SQLite affinity rules are copied: the numeric-affinity matches!, both TEXT-to-numeric coercions through try_coerce_string_to_numeric, and both numeric-to-TEXT branches through format_float_for_text. One private helper in a shared module serves both callers unchanged, and today a fix to SQLite's coercion semantics has to land twice.

position (search.rs:14) and replace (transform.rs:12) are almost entirely the same prelude: an args.len() check raising ExecutorError::UnsupportedFeature with the same format string, then one match coerce_to_string(&args[i]) per argument returning SqlValue::Null on None, with a single line of real payload each. That prelude appears 78 times under evaluator/functions, so one argument-coercion helper parameterized by name and arity would serve them all without changing behavior.

BitwiseOps::or (37) and BitwiseOps::and (46) are three statements each: to_i64_bitwise(left)?, to_i64_bitwise(right)?, then Ok(SqlValue::Integer(l | r)) or Ok(SqlValue::Integer(l & r)). The coercion they share is already factored out into to_i64_bitwise above them, so what remains is a single machine operator per function. Merging them would mean passing an operator token or a closure into an #[inline] wrapper, which is strictly worse than the two three-line bodies.

Read new_function_context at 172 to 177 in crates/vibesql-executor/src/procedural/function.rs beside create_test_db at 17 to 22 in crates/vibesql-executor/src/tests/expression_index_dml_tests.rs: each constructs a value, sets one flag and returns it, over unrelated types (ExecutionContext against Database). The shared body is the three-statement builder idiom whose whole difference is the erased names.

date_to_days_since_epoch at storage.rs:205 and at simd_filter/conversion.rs:57 are byte-identical bodies: same year_days, same three-term leap_years expression, same twelve-arm month_days table, same is_leap test and the same leap_adjustment sum. The storage.rs copy is private while the conversion.rs one is already pub, so the call already compiles with no signature change. Its own doc comment concedes the duplication, saying the function MUST be kept in sync with the other, which is the manual obligation deleting the copy removes.

Read columnar_hash_join_inner at 43 to 82 beside columnar_hash_join_left_outer at 84 to 125 in crates/vibesql-executor/src/select/join/hash_join/columnar/mod.rs: the pair of key-column lookups with their identical ColumnarColumnNotFound construction is repeated in all three functions, and only which side builds the hash table plus the probe and gather callees change. One key-column helper and a join-kind parameter would serve.

parse_drop_assertion (assertion.rs:33) and parse_drop_domain (domain.rs:58) both parse DROP <keyword> <identifier> [CASCADE | RESTRICT] into a two-field statement struct, and the shared clause has already drifted into two spellings (try_consume_keyword(Cascade) then try_consume_keyword(Restrict) versus peek_keyword plus advance), with a third in parse_drop_type (type_def.rs:54). A shared drop-behavior helper would serve every parse_drop_* without changing behavior, and the drift is evidence the repetition is unintended rather than designed.

parse_drop_collation (75) and parse_drop_translation (54) are four lines each: expect_keyword(Drop), expect_keyword(Collation|Translation), parse_identifier()?, and construct DropCollationStmt or DropTranslationStmt from it. The entire difference is the Keyword variant and the AST struct, both erased names, and the two return distinct types the parser dispatches on. A shared version needs a generic or a macro over the statement type to save three lines of the clearest possible statement parser.

Read parse_show_tables at 61 to 90 beside parse_show_databases at 92 to 113 in crates/vibesql-parser/src/parser/introspection.rs: the optional LIKE block and the optional WHERE block are repeated word for word, and only the extra FROM clause and the returned statement struct differ. Two small helpers for the optional clauses would serve both, and parse_show_columns below repeats the same blocks a third time.

find_leftmost_leaf (334) and find_rightmost_leaf (355) repeat the whole descent: start at root_page_id, loop `for _ in 0..self.height - 1`, read_internal_node, return the same StorageError::IoError("Internal node has no children") on an empty children vector, step to a child, then read_leaf_node. The only difference is `internal.children[0]` against `*internal.children.last().unwrap()`. A private descent taking the child selector, or just first()/last(), serves both without behavior change, and it also removes the unwrap the rightmost copy needs, so the empty-children invariant is checked in one place instead of two.

Sender::clone and Receiver::clone each repeat the same overflow invariant (fetch_add on their own counter, then `if count > usize::MAX / 2 { abort() }` with the same comment), which one private helper taking &AtomicUsize would serve for both while each impl keeps its own struct literal.

Buf::get_u8 and Buf::get_i8 repeat the same four-step scaffold (remaining check, panic_advance with requested/available, chunk()[0], advance(1)) differing only by an `as i8` cast, and the file already generates every wider getter through buf_get_impl!, so one macro arm could serve both unchanged.

try_get_u8 and try_get_i8 are the same guard-return-Err/read-chunk/advance/Ok body with a single `as i8` difference, the exact shape buf_try_get_impl! already generates for the wider widths in the same file.

Buf::copy_to_slice for &[u8] and BufMut::put_slice for &mut [u8] are two different traits on two different types, and all they share is the six-line length check that already delegates to the common panic_advance helper: the payload lines copy in opposite directions and only one of them is unsafe, so nothing further is factorable.

Chain::advance and Chain::advance_mut repeat the whole partial-consumption algorithm line for line (a_rem probe, early return when a covers cnt, drain a, subtract, forward the rest to b, comment included), sixteen lines of real logic that one macro emitting both bodies would serve identically.

Limit::advance_mut and Take::advance are three-line delegations (assert cnt <= limit, forward to inner, decrement limit) on two different types in two different traits, one of them unsafe, whose entire difference is the erased method name.

The two ptr_map bodies are #[cfg(miri)] and #[cfg(not(miri))] alternatives of the same function, and the comment above them states they must differ (strict-provenance wrapping_add for miri diagnostics versus `new_addr as *mut u8` for codegen), so no single definition can serve both.

Four separate impl Flag blocks whose update is `let x = convert(v.unwrap_value())?; args.<field>.push(x); Ok(())`, differing in the converter and the destination field: a required trait method per flag type with nothing beyond the two-line delegation to factor.

max-columns and threads both write `let n = convert::<int>(...)?; args.<field> = if n == 0 { None } else { Some(n) }; Ok(())` inside their own Flag impl, a two-line delegation whose difference is the numeric converter and the field it assigns.

help::generate_long and man::generate repeat the same fifteen-line documentation assembly (BTreeMap keyed by doc_category, iterate FLAGS, insert a separator between entries, render each flag, then replace !!VERSION!! and one !!CATEGORY!! variable per key in a template), which one function parameterized by template, separator and per-flag writer would serve without behavior change.

PrefixStrategy::is_match and SuffixStrategy::is_match wrap the same AhoCorasick overlapping-match scan over a bounded slice of the candidate, with only the anchor varying (path_prefix + m.start() == 0 versus path_suffix + m.end() == path.len()); the two structs carry identical fields, so one type generic over the anchor would serve both.

PrefixStrategy::matches_all and SuffixStrategy::matches_all repeat the same counting scan and the `count == self.map.len()` conclusion, comment included, with only the anchor predicate differing, so the same anchor parameter that unifies the is_match pair would serve these two unchanged.

WalkBuilder::max_depth and min_depth are a by-design mirrored setter pair: the assigned field and the comparison direction are inverted (max<min raises max, min>max lowers min), so the only factoring is a four-line clamp helper carrying a direction flag, which serves neither call site more clearly.

ByteSet::add and remove have three-line bodies whose two shared lines are the bucket/bit computation and whose difference is the actual bit operation (|= 1<<bit versus &= !(1<<bit)), so nothing but erased-name boilerplate is common.

These are two distinct serde::Serialize impls, for Begin and for End, serializing different struct names and different field sets (one field versus three), so the language forces them apart and only the SerializeStruct boilerplate is shared.

AstAnalysis::from_ast and non_matching_bytes are three-line constructor delegations in different crates whose entire difference lives in the erased names (AstAnalysis::new/from_ast_impl versus ByteSet::full/remove_matching_bytes); there is no shared scaffold to factor.

is_good and is_really_good repeat the same five-line guard verbatim (the has_poisonous_literal early return plus the two let-else extractions of min_literal_len and len) before diverging only in the threshold predicate, and one private accessor returning Option<(min, len)> would serve both without changing behavior.

deserialize_bool and deserialize_unit share the seven-line parse_whitespace/peek_error prologue and the four-line fix_position epilogue verbatim around a keyword match, and the same file already factors exactly this shape with the deserialize_number! macro, so a macro can serve both.

The two hi64_1 bodies live in separate trait impls the language forces apart, Hi64<u32> for [u32] and Hi64<u64> for [u64], and their three lines differ by the `as u64` widening cast the u32 limb needs.

mul and add are four-line owned-copy wrappers over imul and iadd whose entire difference is the in-place function called and its second argument type, a short delegation with nothing but the Vec-copy boilerplate in common.

Number's arbitrary_precision serialize and RawValue's serialize are separate Serialize impls for separate types, each a three-line one-field serialize_struct delegation differing only in the field it hands over (self.n versus self.json).

The two end_raw_buffering bodies are distinct Read trait impls for the owned and borrowed readers: one takes a Vec and calls String::from_utf8 into OwnedRawDeserializer, the other slices self.slice and calls str::from_utf8 into BorrowedRawDeserializer under a different lifetime, so ownership forces them apart.

The two `end` methods belong to separate impls, SerializeTupleVariant and SerializeStructVariant, and each is a four-line body wrapping its own payload (Value::Array(self.vec) versus Value::Object(self.map)) into a one-entry Map.

take_int and take_ident repeat a nine-line scaffold verbatim (the length counter, the char loop with a match arm that increments or breaks, the split_at, the advance of *read and the return) and differ only in the accepted char pattern, which one take_while taking a char predicate serves without changing behavior.
src/code/mod.rs declares only executor and highlight while its doc comment promises PTY support, so pty.rs was meant to be wired in and is not.
index_optimization/mod.rs declares only mod spatial, and the only mod order_by in the crate is in select/window/mod.rs, so this file is dead.
arena_parser/mod.rs declares ddl, delete, expression, insert, select and update but no mod dml, and no other declaration reaches the file.
parser/mod.rs lists twenty-four submodules with no mod type_def, and the only similar declaration is in the separate vibesql-catalog crate.
lib.rs declares no mod modules, so modules/mod.rs is unreachable and database.rs under it is dead.
lib.rs declares pub mod examples resolving to the top-level src/examples.rs, leaving the parallel modules/examples.rs unreachable.
lib.rs resolves pub mod execute to src/execute.rs, and no declaration reaches modules/execute.rs.
no file in the crate declares mod modules, so modules/mod.rs itself is compiled by nothing.
lib.rs resolves pub mod query to src/query.rs, and no declaration reaches modules/query.rs.
lib.rs resolves pub mod schema to src/schema.rs, and no declaration reaches modules/schema.rs.
modules/types.rs is reachable only through the orphaned modules/mod.rs, so nothing compiles it.

run_sync chains nine banner-commented phases in one body: meter, display and pattern_gen connection, session creation, patch generation, the measurement loop, grayscale analysis, 1D LUT generation, the tiered 3D LUT with its Alpha 7 downsample, and upload plus completion. Each phase sets its own CalibrationState and touches distinct collaborators, so extracting them is mechanical.

generate_instruction is a single exhaustive match over the Instruction enum: roughly 45 arms, each one to four lines that call one cg.emit_* method and, for the second half, one cg.state().reg_cache.invalidate_all(). No arm nests logic worth extracting, and the only visible seam (the 'acc-preserving' versus 'cache-invalidating' comment banners) cannot be turned into two functions without replacing the exhaustive match with a fallthrough one, which is exactly what makes a new Instruction variant compile-error today. The length here is the arity of the IR instruction set, not a missing decomposition.

The file holds one impl block with 36 encoder methods, and its own header enumerates the families it stacks (MOV, LEA, PUSH/POP, ALU, TEST, IMUL, shifts, bit operations, setcc/cmovcc, jumps, calls, exchange). The encoder directory already splits by family into sse.rs, system.rs, x87.rs and registers.rs, all under 400 lines, so the same split applies here.

emit_cast_instrs_impl matches on CastKind, but the same three RISC-V extension sequences are typed out verbatim over and over inside the arms: 'slli t0,t0,56 / srai t0,t0,56' three times, 'slli 48 / srai 48' three times, 'slli 48 / srli 48' three times, 'slli 32 / srli 32' three times, 'andi t0,t0,0xff' four times and 'sext.w t0,t0' four times. Two helpers keyed on IrType, one sign-extending and one zero-extending or truncating, would serve the inner matches of FloatToSigned, FloatToUnsigned, SignedToFloat, SignedToUnsignedSameSize, IntWiden and IntNarrow and cut roughly a hundred lines to about twenty-five. The factoring is behavior-preserving and is the natural shape for a codegen backend.

substitute_riscv_asm_operands is a hand-rolled character scanner taking nine parallel operand slices, and its while loop carries five independent branches: %z[name], %zN, %lo and %hi passthrough, %[name] and positional %N. The %z handling alone runs about 65 lines and duplicates the name lookup the %[name] branch performs, so both a helper per modifier and an operand struct are available.

combined_local_pass is one while loop carrying seven patterns that the module doc comment already enumerates by number and that the body already separates with '--- Pattern: ... ---' banners: self-move, reverse-move, redundant jump, conditional-branch inversion, adjacent store/load, redundant extension and redundant xorl. Each block reads only store, infos, i and len and signals its result through mark_nop plus 'changed', so each becomes a fn(store, &mut infos, i) -> bool, and the sixty-line rax_is_zero state machine becomes its own update function. That keeps the single linear scan the merge was written for, which is the only rationale the doc comment gives for the size.

Despite its name, types.rs holds three concerns: the LineInfo, LineKind, ExtKind and MoveSize declarations (lines 11 to 200), the classification pass (classify_line, classify_mov_ext, classify_arith_ext, about 320 lines), and roughly thirty free utilities including register_family_fast, REG_NAMES, scan_register_refs, memrchr and write_rbp_pattern. The peephole directory already has a passes subdirectory to model the split on.

The file's own header says the parser is split into expressions.rs, types.rs, statements.rs, declarations.rs and declarators.rs, each adding pub(super) methods to Parser, yet parse.rs still carries three unrelated clusters beyond the Parser struct and parse(): the whole GCC __attribute__ family (parse_gcc_attribute_list, dispatch_gcc_attribute, and the cleanup/mode/vector_size/ext_vector_type/address_space handlers, lines 684-950), the pragma handling (handle_pragma_pack_token, handle_pragma_visibility_token), and the static sizeof/alignof type-spec helpers (try_sizeof_type_spec, alignof_type_spec, preferred_alignof_type_spec). Moving the attribute cluster alone to an attributes.rs impl block is mechanical under the convention the module already uses and takes the file well under a thousand lines.

The file mixes a 275-line parse_type_specifier flag collector with a separate struct, union and enum group (parse_struct_or_union, parse_struct_field_declarators, consume_struct_field_qualifiers, parse_enum_specifier) that runs about 300 lines and shares nothing but the Parser receiver. Sibling modules declarators.rs, statements.rs and expressions.rs show the parser is already split along exactly this kind of seam.

try_lower_builtin_call is a chain of independent special cases before the final resolve_builtin dispatch: the user-definition override with its SSE exception, __builtin_choose_expr, the alloca match, the three-arm va_start/va_end/va_copy match, __builtin_expect, __builtin_prefetch, __builtin_unreachable and __builtin_trap. Each returns Option<Operand> and touches only self, name and args, so each extracts unchanged. The file already sets that precedent: lower_builtin_intrinsic sits right below it, extracted from the BuiltinKind::Intrinsic arm of this very function.

lower_function_call runs sequential, independently testable phases: stripping no-op Deref layers, unwrapping AddressOf on a function name, resolving _Generic selections, dispatching __builtin_ and error-attribute functions, computing the sret and two-register return convention, lowering arguments with implicit casts and complex decomposition, then emitting the call. Each phase reads only the expression and produces one named value.

structs.rs holds two responsibilities that never call into each other: type registration and layout computation (register_struct_type, register_nested_struct_types, recompute_vector_struct_layouts, struct_layout_key, union_layout_key, mark_transparent_union, lines 19-345) and member-access resolution (the resolve_member_access / resolve_member_access_full / resolve_member_access_with_ctype trio with their _impl bodies, get_layout_for_expr, resolve_field_struct_layout, resolve_func_call_struct_layout, lines 608-1050), with the 215-line get_struct_base_addr between them. The sibling lowering module is already split this way into twenty-five files by responsibility, including struct_init.rs for the initializer half, so a struct_access.rs split follows the crate's own convention rather than inventing one.

compute_decl_info returns a five-element tuple (alloc_size, elem_size, is_array, is_pointer, array_dim_strides) and branches into four self-contained size computations: simple or typedef pointer, array of pointers including the function-pointer-array dim ordering, pointer to array with its trailing-pointer counting, and the plain array or scalar case. Each branch is a nameable helper and the tuple is a struct waiting to be declared.

main is a match over roughly thirty Commands variants, and the arms are inconsistent: Epd, DumpBinpack and SplitBinpack are three-line delegations to epd::run_epd, run_dump_binpack and run_split_binpack, while EvalBench inlines about two hundred lines of NNUE loading, EPD parsing, warm-up and timing, Bench inlines the whole --set tunable parsing loop plus the multi-threaded spawn/join, and InspectBinpack, PatchNet and DumpThreats inline eighty to ninety lines each. Extracting run_eval_bench and its peers as free functions is exactly what the file already does for the binpack commands, and it takes main back to the dispatch it is supposed to be.

movepicker.rs stacks four independent units plus tests: the History tables with their bonus and aging math (lines 21 to 186), the staged MovePicker itself (188 to 920), a 200-line is_pseudo_legal validator that touches no picker state, QMovePicker (1180 to 1326), and six separate test modules from line 1327 on. History and is_pseudo_legal are natural sibling files.

export_html interleaves three separable things in one body: an 85-line CSS raw-string literal, a 30-line navigation JavaScript raw-string literal, and the per-slide render loop whose six sections (title/subtitle, bullets, code blocks, block quotes, tables, image data-URI, notes) each push into the same String. Hoisting the two literals to consts and lifting the loop body to fn render_slide(&Slide) -> String leaves the entry point at roughly forty lines with no behavior change, since the only shared state is the html accumulator. Nothing here is forced by a trait contract; escape_html already sits beside it as a free helper.

apply_font_change bundles two independent strategies plus a resize drain: the slide path builds a full-screen buffer, computes Kitty font stepping parameters, and runs a dissolve loop nested five levels deep (frame, row, span, char, cell padding) while interleaving font step batches, and the plain path then switches on font_capability. The dissolve frame renderer alone is an obvious extraction.

create_tpcc_schema_vibesql is nine consecutive db.create_table(TableSchema::with_primary_key(...)).unwrap() statements for warehouse, district, customer, history, new_order, orders, order_line, item and stock, with no branching, no loop and no state beyond the varchar() closure. The length is the arity of the TPC-C schema itself, about ninety ColumnSchema::new lines whose column names and types all differ, so there is nothing to factor and a split into nine single-statement functions would add indirection without removing anything. The flat declarative sequence is the clearest form and matches the sibling MySQL schema function in the same file.

The TableSchema impl runs 45 methods across four unrelated groups: six with_* builder constructors (with_primary_key through with_all_constraint_types), read accessors (get_column, column_count, primary_key_effective_collations), column mutations (add_column, remove_column, rename_column, set_column_nullable, set_column_default), and constraint mutations (add and drop for check, unique and foreign key). Splitting into per-concern impl blocks changes no call site.

process_constraints is two independent phases against one accumulator: the column-level loop matching ColumnConstraintKind over roughly a hundred and ten lines, then the table-level loop matching TableConstraintKind over sixty-five, sharing only `result` and the has_column_level_pk flag that the first phase alone owns. Each phase extracts to a function taking table_name, columns and &mut ConstraintResult, and each keeps its own exhaustive match, so no compile-time coverage is lost. The file already hosts free helpers of that shape next door: dedup_pk_key_parts, key_part_collations and validate_check_expression.

check_child_references_impl is two phases joined by one vector: a 140-line collection loop over every catalog table and each of its foreign keys, extracting parent key values and scanning the child table under an MVCC snapshot, followed by a 100-line dispatch matching Restrict, NoAction, Cascade, SetNull and SetDefault. The intermediate actions_to_perform tuple is already the seam between them.

hash_expression is a single exhaustive match over the ~40 variants of vibesql_ast::Expression, and every arm is variant-specific field enumeration (ColumnRef hashes table_canonical/column_canonical, Between hashes expr/low/high/negated/symmetric, MatchAgainst hashes columns then search_modifier then mode). There is no repeated scaffold to factor: the length is exactly the number of AST variants times the fields each one carries. Splitting it into hash_subquery/hash_temporal groups would force the outer arms to keep naming the variants and then re-match inside, and would give up the one place where the compiler's exhaustiveness check catches a newly added Expression variant.

eval_between opens with three dispatch prologues (row value constructor operands, scalar subquery against row-value bounds, the mixed row-value misuse check), then defines a 35-line transform_for_collation closure handling NOCASE and RTRIM over four SqlValue variants, then runs affinity resolution and the reversed-bounds and negation comparisons. The collation transform is a pure function that belongs beside the other collation helpers.

deserialize_value's bulk is mechanical boilerplate, not dispatch: the INTEGER, SMALLINT, BIGINT, UNSIGNED, NUMERIC, FLOAT, REAL and DOUBLE arms are eight copies of `let mut buf = [0u8; N]; reader.read_exact(&mut buf)?; Ok(...::from_le_bytes(buf))`, and CHARACTER/VARCHAR, INTERVAL, VECTOR and BLOB each re-spell the same `read u32 length, then read that many bytes` prologue. A `read_le::<N>(reader)` helper and a `read_len_prefixed(reader)` helper collapse those twelve arms to one or two lines each and take the function well under the bound, leaving the tag dispatch itself untouched. The DATE and TIMESTAMP arms, which carry the real logic (the from_parts_unchecked leniency comment), also stop being buried in byte plumbing.

try_extract_subqueries_to_joins carries two blocks of about 45 lines each, one for the left operand and one for the right of the And arm, that repeat the same In, Exists and scalar-comparison dispatch with only the sibling expression swapped, followed by two more symmetric recursive branches. One helper taking the candidate side and its remainder collapses all four.

The 2268 lines carry no test module at all: it is all production code, and it holds at least four independent concerns that already sit in contiguous runs. Table-reference discovery (collect_stmt_table_refs, collect_from_table_refs, collect_expr_table_refs at 724-1038 plus stmt_references_table, from_clause_references_table, expr_references_table at 2137-2268), wildcard expansion (WildcardColumn, WildcardSource, visible_columns, view_column_names, expand_wildcard_names, collect_from_sources, collect_select_list_columns at 1096-1371) and the recursive-CTE machinery (RecursiveSplit, split_recursive_compound, execute_recursive_cte, execute_recursive_frontier, execute_recursive_queue at 1371-1980) each move to a cte/refs.rs, cte/wildcard.rs and cte/recursive.rs with no signature change, leaving execute_ctes and execute_cte_at in the parent.

evaluate is a single 569-line match over Expression whose arms are fully independent: Cast recurses then calls cast_value, Between reimplements symmetric bound swapping and three-valued logic, InList runs its own NULL bookkeeping loop, and Like re-derives text coercion across the SqlValue variants. Each arm is 50 to 150 lines and depends only on its own sub-expressions, so one function per arm is the direct decomposition.

execute_with_iterators is already written as labeled stages and the seams are named in its own comments: the ExecutionContext assembly (outer_row/procedural/trigger/cte/outer_rows, ~25 lines), Stage 2's five-arm WhereOptimization match, Stage 3 and 4's OFFSET/LIMIT boxing, and Stage 6's SIMD-or-row-by-row projection (~40 lines). Each is a self-contained extraction over values it already computes (schema, evaluator, filtered_rows), for instance a build_evaluation_context(&self, &schema) -> Evaluator and a project_rows(&self, &filtered_rows, stmt, &evaluator, &schema). Nothing here is forced by a trait contract; the function is long because six pipeline stages were inlined into one body.

extract_column_refs is an exhaustive visitor over the Expression enum: every arm is one to three recursive calls, and the tail lists the terminal variants (Literal, Wildcard, CurrentDate, Placeholder and friends) explicitly with no wildcard arm. The length is set by the width of the AST, not by logic, and splitting the match would surrender the exhaustiveness check that forces every new variant to be handled.

The twelve arms of resolve_aliases_in_expression repeat one concrete scaffold: call resolve_alias_or_clone on each child, set an any_resolved flag, then rebuild the variant with unwrap_or_else(|| child.as_ref().clone()) on every unresolved child, else return None. Between spends 20 lines on three children, InList and Function spend 20 more each on the same flag-tracking closure, and Case spends 60. A single `fn resolve_child(child, select_list, any: &mut bool) -> Expression` returning the clone when nothing resolved reduces every one of those arms to a two- to five-line rebuild and removes the hand-written flag bookkeeping that is currently duplicated in five closures.

start_calibration and end_calibration in LgDeviceControlClient are byte-identical except the endpoint path, and they repeat the same POST-json/send/map_err/status-check/Ok scaffold that connect, upload_1d_lut and set_white_balance also carry. DeviceControlClient::display_pattern in hal-patterns repeats the same scaffold with PatternGenError instead of DisplayError. A private post_json(path, body) helper per client (or one generic over the error constructor) would serve every member without changing behavior.

encode_neon_float_two_misc and encode_neon_float_cmp_zero have the same signature, the same arrangement match (2s/4s/2d), the same size computation and the same word layout; only the error-message text differs. Both encode the identical AArch64 two-register-misc float format, so one function (or one calling the other) would serve both call sites without changing any encoded word.

f128_flip_sign_bit is a trait method implemented once per backend: the ARM version emits mov/eor/mov on v0.d[1], the RISC-V version emits li/slli/xor on a1. The bodies are three self.state.emit calls whose entire content is the architecture-specific assembly literal, which the normalizer erases; there is no shared scaffold to factor between two backends the trait deliberately keeps apart. A minimal crate with two impls of one trait, each method making three emit calls with different string literals, would reproduce this misjudgment as a regression seed.

encode_cmpxchg and encode_xadd are line-for-line identical: same operand-count check, same size suffix, same (Register, Memory) match with the 0x66 prefix, emit_rex_rm, 0x0F escape and encode_modrm_mem; they differ only in the opcode pair (0xB0/0xB1 vs 0xC0/0xC1) and the mnemonic in error strings. One helper taking the mnemonic name and the two opcode bytes would serve both without changing the emitted bytes.

add_weight_rows_avx2 and add_weight_rows_avx512 are per-ISA SIMD kernels under different #[target_feature] attributes; the doc comment on the AVX-512 one states it mirrors the AVX2 one by design. Every operation differs in the erased names: __m256i vs __m512i, _mm256_loadu/cvtepi8/add/storeu vs their _mm512 counterparts, 16 vs 32 lanes per register. Merging them would need a macro parameterized over roughly eight intrinsics and types in a hot path, which obscures each kernel for no behavioral gain. A minimal crate with two #[target_feature] functions differing only in intrinsic names and a lane-width literal would reproduce this misjudgment as a regression seed.

BenchStats::print in vibesql-bench-common and in vibesql-storage/benches/harness.rs are identical, and the bench file's header says it is a simplified copy of the shared harness, with from_times and BenchConfig copied too. vibesql-bench-common is the workspace's shared benchmark crate and its default features pull only rand, so vibesql-storage could take it as a dev-dependency and use the one definition. Because print is documented as a format consumed by benchmark parsers, keeping two copies risks silent drift; one definition would serve both without changing output.

The two update_state methods share a now-in-millis computation and the terminal-state match, but the rest is store-specific SQL: profiling_sessions sets ended_at only, while sessions also maintains updated_at, so the statements and parameter lists differ in arity on both branches. What would be factored is a four-line timestamp idiom and a one-line predicate; a shared update_state would need two SQL strings and differently-sized params, which adds indirection to two parallel stores that have already diverged in schema. A minimal crate with two functions of identical control flow whose only differences are SQL literals and params arity would reproduce this misjudgment, since literal normalization hides the part that carries the semantics.

encode_cset and encode_csetm share the whole body: parse rd, parse the condition operand, invert it, and assemble the conditional-select word with XZR in Rn and Rm. They differ only in the op bit (1 << 30) and the o2 field (0b01 << 10), i.e. CSINC vs CSINV, plus the mnemonic in the error string. One helper taking op and o2 (shared with the csel/csinc/csinv/csneg family) would serve both without changing any encoding.

encode_cnt, encode_neon_not and encode_neon_rev64 repeat the same two-register-misc scaffold (operand check, two get_neon_reg calls, Q from the arrangement, 0 Q U 01110 size 10000 opcode 10 Rn Rd word), and the same file already defines encode_neon_two_misc for exactly that format: CNT is U=0, opcode 00101, NOT is U=1, opcode 00101, REV64 is U=0, opcode 00000. encode_neon_bic and encode_neon_bsl are likewise one three-same logical encoding differing in the U bit. The members could delegate to the existing helper or one sibling helper without changing any encoded word.

The two parse_instruction functions live in the AArch64 and RISC-V assembler parsers and each builds its own module's AsmStatement and calls its own parse_operands, which in RISC-V takes the mnemonic as a second argument. The only logic actually shared is a five-line split of the mnemonic at the first space or tab; one definition cannot serve both without generic plumbing over two unrelated statement types. A minimal crate with two modules each defining a same-named enum and parse_operands, wrapped by an identical-looking function, would reproduce this misjudgment as a regression seed, since name normalization cannot see that the types differ.

emit_i128_neg_impl exists once per backend: ARM emits mvn/mvn/adds/adc, RISC-V emits not/not/addi/seqz/add. The bodies are sequences of self.state.emit calls whose whole content is the architecture's assembly literals, which the normalizer erases; nothing is shared but the call to emit. A minimal crate with two inherent impls on different types, each emitting a few different string literals through the same method, would reproduce this misjudgment as a regression seed.

emit_jcc_block, emit_instr_imm and emit_instr_rbp are #[inline] fast-path emitters that each push a fixed shape into the buffer without format!: they differ in the separator literals (" .LBB", " $", "(%rbp)"), in which integer writer they call (write_u64_fast vs write_i64_fast) and in operand order. Each body is four or five push calls; the difference lives entirely in literals and callee names, and a shared helper would just be a format string interpreter undoing the reason they exist. A minimal crate with three methods that push different string literals and call different integer writers would reproduce this misjudgment as a regression seed.

emit_int_cmp_impl in the i686 and x86-64 backends share the same ten-arm IrCmpOp to setcc mnemonic table and the same set/zero-extend/invalidate/store tail; they differ only in the compare prelude and the eax vs rax register names. The repository has src/backend/x86_common.rs whose header states it exists to share condition code mappings between exactly these two backends, so moving the IrCmpOp-to-setcc table there is a change the project's own design asks for, with no behavior change.

encode_alu_reg, encode_fp_sgnj and encode_fmv_x_f are four-line RISC-V encoders that already delegate the word layout to the shared encode_r; what remains is fetching operands with the register-class getter the format requires (get_reg vs get_freg), the opcode constant (OP_OP vs OP_OP_FP) and a fixed funct3. The entire difference lives in those erased names, so there is no scaffold left to factor. A minimal crate with three short functions that call different getters and pass different constants to one shared builder would reproduce this misjudgment as a regression seed.

encode_v_arith_vx and encode_v_arith_vi are the OPIVX and OPIVI encoders: they differ exactly in what the format distinguishes, the third operand (scalar register via get_reg vs 5-bit immediate via get_imm masked to 0x1F) and funct3 (100 vs 011). The shared remainder is one word-assembly expression; factoring it would leave each function nearly as long and hide the per-format layout each doc comment documents. A minimal crate with two seven-line functions differing in one callee and one literal would reproduce this misjudgment as a regression seed.

emit_fused_cmp_branch_impl and emit_fused_cmp_branch_blocks_impl share the same use_32bit computation, the same emit_int_cmp_insn_typed call and the same ten-arm IrCmpOp to jcc table (the second one only prefixes each mnemonic with four spaces), then differ in emitting to labels vs block ids. A single IrCmpOp-to-jcc helper (with emit_jcc_block taking a bare mnemonic) would serve both without changing emitted assembly, removing a duplicated condition-code table that must stay in sync.

handle_if and handle_elif run the same five-step #if expression pipeline: resolve_defined_in_expr, expand_line_reuse, resolve_defined_in_expr again, replace_remaining_idents_with_zero and evaluate_condition; they differ only in the last call (push_if vs handle_elif). The comment in handle_elif ("same reason as handle_if") already records the coupling. Extracting an eval_if_condition(expr) -> bool method would serve both without changing behavior and keep the C semantics in one place.

read_u8 and read_u16 are three-line binary readers that differ in the return type, the buffer size and the conversion (buf[0] vs u16::from_le_bytes). The entire difference lives in types and literals; std offers no trait over from_le_bytes, so unifying them needs a macro or a third-party crate for a three-line body. A minimal crate with two such typed read helpers would reproduce this misjudgment as a regression seed.

vibesql-executor's visit_statement rebuilds the same private ClosureVisitor, the same ExpressionVisitor and StatementVisitor impls and the same walk_statement call as vibesql_ast::visitor::visit_expressions; the only difference is holding the closure as &mut F instead of F. Since &mut F is itself FnMut(&Expression), visit_statement can be a one-line call to visit_expressions(stmt, visitor) without changing behavior, and the executor module's own doc says it is a convenience wrapper around the ast visitor.

load_lineitem_sqlite and load_lineitem_duckdb repeat the full TPC-H lineitem generation: the order/line loop, part and supplier key formulas, quantity, price, discount, tax, three random dates and the flag/mode selections; they differ only in the connection type and rusqlite::params! vs duckdb::params!. The members are not a comparison pair of the code under measurement but data loaders whose generated rows must be identical across engines for the comparison to be fair, so a shared row generator (iterator yielding the computed fields, consumed by each engine) would serve both without changing behavior and remove a drift risk.

The DELETE fast path execute_truncate and truncate::core::execute_truncate share the table lookup, row_count, table.clear(), database.rebuild_indexes and columnar-cache invalidation; the delete-side comment says the rebuild_indexes call was added after spurious UNIQUE errors because "the TRUNCATE TABLE executor does the same", i.e. the copies already drifted once. A shared clear_table_contents(database, table_name) -> Result<usize> with each caller adding its own tail (assertion checks vs AUTO_INCREMENT reset) would serve both without changing behavior.

st_geom_from_text and st_point_from_text repeat the same argument-count check, the same Varchar/Character/Null extraction and the same parse_wkt call, differing only in the function name in error messages and the POINT check in the second. A helper returning the parsed geometry or NULL for a given function name would serve both (and the sibling *FromText constructors) without changing behavior.

map_branch_conjunct and map_conjunct are the same 120-line whitelist rewriter over Expression; the branch version's doc comment says it mirrors map_conjunct, and the only differences are the context type (BranchPushContext vs PushContext, both exposing resolve_column) and comments. Making the walker generic over a small trait with resolve_column would serve both without changing behavior, and keeps a safety-relevant whitelist (what may be pushed below a window or UNION ALL) from drifting between copies.

string_to_truthy in select/executor/arena_execution.rs is the same SQLite string-to-boolean conversion as string_to_truthy in select/filter.rs, statement for statement, minus comments and with map/unwrap_or in place of a match. Both are private functions in the same crate, so making one pub(crate) and calling it from the other serves both without changing behavior and keeps one definition of a SQLite semantics rule.

parse_expression_sql and parse_alter_table_sql both build a Lexer, call tokenize() with the identical map_err closure formatting "Lexer error: {}", and construct ArenaParser::new(tokens, arena); they differ only in the final parser method called (and the arena.alloc wrap). The same lex-and-construct scaffold is copied into more than a dozen sibling entry points in this impl (parse_insert, parse_update, parse_delete, parse_replace and their _with_interner variants). One private helper returning the ready ArenaParser would serve every member without changing behavior, so the repeated error-mapping scaffold is worth factoring.

Deserialize for Level and Deserialize for LevelFilter each define an identifier Visitor (expecting, visit_u64, visit_str, visit_bytes), a DeserializeSeed impl, and an enum Visitor with visit_enum, about 75 lines each with the same control flow. The only differences are the target type, the expecting string, and whether the names slice is LOG_LEVEL_NAMES[1..] or LOG_LEVEL_NAMES. Both types implement FromStr, so one generic visitor parameterized by the names slice and expecting text (or a small macro) would serve both impls without changing behavior; the duplicated scaffold is nontrivial, not a short delegation.

The three members are the Flag::update methods of the CaseSensitive, Files and TypeList flag structs: each is an assert on v.unwrap_switch(), a single field assignment (args.case = CaseMode::Sensitive, args.mode.update(Mode::Files), args.mode.update(Mode::Types)), and Ok(()). The bodies are three lines whose entire difference is which field is set, and each lives in a separate trait impl that ripgrep's flag design requires per flag; there is no scaffold to factor. A minimal crate with one trait and three impls whose short method bodies differ only in the assigned field could reproduce this as a regression seed.

The members are the Flag::update impls for LineNumber, NoConfig and NullData: an assert on v.unwrap_switch() with a message, one or two field assignments (args.line_number = Some(true), args.no_config = true, args.crlf = false plus args.null_data = true), then Ok(()). Each is a separate trait impl the flag registry requires, and the bodies are too short to share anything beyond the trait signature; the difference lives entirely in the fields written. A minimal crate with several trait impls whose three-line bodies assign different fields could reproduce this as a regression seed.

shr and shl are mirrored five-line primitives on ExtendedFloat: shr does fp.mant >>= shift and fp.exp += shift, shl does fp.mant <<= shift and fp.exp -= shift, each with a debug_assert bound. The whole difference is the shift direction and the sign of the exponent update, which are exactly what the normalization treats as near-equal; merging them behind a direction parameter would obscure two textbook operations and add a branch on a hot inline path. A minimal crate with a paired shift-left/shift-right helper differing only in operators could reproduce this as a regression seed.

Deserialize for Number defines a NumberVisitor with visit_i64, visit_i128, visit_u64, visit_u128, visit_f64 and a cfg-gated visit_map, then calls deserialize_any; Deserialize for &RawValue defines a ReferenceVisitor with only visit_map ending in next_value_seed(ReferenceFromString), then calls deserialize_newtype_struct(TOKEN, ...). What they share is the serde Visitor boilerplate the trait contract imposes plus the RawKey/NumberKey map-key check, and they deserialize different types through different Deserializer entry points, so there is no common definition that would serve both. A minimal crate with two Deserialize impls whose local visitors share the serde skeleton, one a superset of the other, could probably reproduce this as a regression seed.

generation.rs mixes three separable responsibilities: per-function analysis prepasses (build_gep_fold_map, build_global_addr_map, build_foldable_global_addr_set, build_global_addr_ptr_set, count_value_uses, detect_cmp_branch_fusion, roughly lines 52 to 487), module-level emission (generate_module and the emit_* section helpers), and function/instruction dispatch (generate_function, generate_instruction, generate_terminator). The analysis helpers take only an IrFunction and return maps, so moving them to a sibling module is mechanical and matches how the backend is already split into many files. The file is not data-like, and the split would plausibly be accepted.

The 1062-line parser.rs holds the AST type definitions (Operand, DataValue, Directive, AsmStatement, lines 19 to 186), a directive parser with its section/type/size/data-value helpers (parse_directive through parse_symbol_addend, lines 325 to 772), and the instruction/operand parser (parse_instruction through parse_int_literal, lines 773 onward). These are independent seams connected only through the AST types, so moving the types or the directive parsing to a sibling file is straightforward and would bring the file under the threshold. The file is barely over the bound, but the split is clean and conventional for an assembler front end.

eval_const_int_expr_with_enums is a match over Expr, but two arms are self-contained computations with narrow inputs: the BinaryOp arm nests a 50-line match over BinOp with four near-identical signed/unsigned relational branches (Lt, Le, Gt, Ge), and the Cast arm carries 35 lines of width truncation and sign extension. Extracting fold_binop(op, l, r, unsigned) and a truncate-to-type helper is mechanical, removes the relational duplication, and leaves the top-level match as a readable dispatcher. Such a refactor would plausibly be accepted.

lower_cast is a sequence of independent early-return cases: complex-to/from-real casts, the GCC cast-to-union extension with alloca and memcpy, cast-to-struct passthrough, vector-to-scalar, scalar-to-vector, vector-to-vector, then the scalar path with _Bool normalization. Each block depends only on target_ctype, inner_ctype and inner, so extracting lower_complex_cast, lower_union_cast and lower_vector_cast is mechanical, and the codebase already uses that style (real_to_complex, complex_to_complex). Decomposition is feasible and would plausibly be accepted.

lower_local_struct_init interleaves anonymous-member drilling, complex-field memcpy, struct-from-sret copies, char-array string literals, array-of-struct flat initializers and scalar-array flat initializers in one loop nested five levels deep, mutating item_idx from several branches. The array-field cases (lines 736 to 815) are separable into a helper that returns the number of items consumed, the same contract emit_struct_init already uses in this branch, and the anonymous-member and complex-field cases extract the same way. Decomposition is feasible and would make the item-consumption logic auditable.

simplify_binop computes a few operand facts (lhs_zero, rhs_one, same_value, is_float) and then runs one flat match over IrBinOp whose arms are lists of algebraic identities, each commented and each returning a rewritten Instruction; the heavier rewrites are already delegated to try_reassociate_*, try_mul_power_of_two and const_power_of_two. Splitting per opcode would push the same seven inputs and precomputed facts into a dozen functions without separating any responsibility, so the flat rule table is the clearest available form. A minimal crate with a long peephole-style match over an operator enum whose arms are short early-return rules could reproduce this as a regression seed.

MdrApp::ui runs five distinct phases in one body: reloading the file on watcher events, F10/Ctrl+F/Escape key handling, the search bar panel with match navigation, the TOC side panel, and the central scroll area. The search bar alone is about 85 lines and repeats the search-reset sequence three times. The eframe::App contract only fixes the ui signature, not its length, and extracting reload_if_changed, show_search_bar, show_toc and show_content methods is the usual egui structure and would plausibly be accepted.

mutation.rs carries a full AST walk for positional parameters (bind_select_mut through bind_frame_bound_mut, lines 35 to 460) and then a second, near-identical walk for named parameters under #[cfg(test)] (bind_select_named_mut through bind_frame_bound_named_mut, lines 461 to 869), each with its own bind_expression body of roughly 170 lines. One walk parameterized by a placeholder resolver (a closure or small trait taking the slice or the map) would serve both and roughly halve the file, or at minimum the test-only walk could move to its own module. Decomposition is feasible and would plausibly be accepted.

execute_scalar_subquery_rows contains the same four-way SelectExecutor construction ladder (outer_rows with or without cte_context, else cte_context, else plain outer context) three times: in the no-correlation-values fallback, in the outer_schema-only branch, and in the cache-miss branch, each 30 to 40 lines. A single helper that builds the executor from the merged row and schema would remove two copies and leave the function as cache-key selection plus cache lookup. Decomposition is feasible and plainly beneficial.

execute_insert_internal is a single 1641-line function running sequential phases: system-table and privilege checks, CTE materialization, view dispatch, schema and trigger resolution, ON CONFLICT target validation, row source resolution (line 402), per-row validation into validated_rows (line 536), then the insert loop, upsert handling and RETURNING. Each phase hands explicit values to the next, so extraction into phase functions is feasible, and a function of this size is unreviewable as a unit. Decomposition would plausibly be accepted.

evaluate_predicate_i64_simd repeats the same SQLite-affinity scaffold in the LessThan, GreaterThan, Equal and NotEqual arms: parse a string threshold as f64 or return a constant via apply_null_mask_constant, use the i64 kernel for Integer and Bigint, else convert via value_to_f64 with an identical ColumnarTypeMismatch error and widen values to f64. The arms differ only in the simd_ops function pair and the constant returned for a non-numeric string. One helper taking the i64 kernel, the f64 kernel and that constant would serve every comparison arm without changing behavior.

execute_via_pipeline combines an eligibility analysis (eight has_* flags and three early fallbacks, lines 1330 to 1400), FROM execution and ExecutionContext construction, WHERE alias resolution, and three pipeline stages that each repeat the same match mapping UnsupportedFeature or UnsupportedExpression to a logged Ok(None). Extracting the eligibility check, the context builder and a small fallback helper for the stage errors is mechanical and keeps the generic pipeline contract intact. Decomposition is feasible and would plausibly be accepted.

join/mod.rs declares ten submodules (including nested_loop and hash_join) yet still holds the FromData/FromResult types and iterator, combine_rows and apply_post_join_filter, the 950-line nested_loop_join dispatcher (lines 474 to 1424), and the USING/NATURAL column coalescing helpers. The nested_loop_join body has an obvious home in the existing nested_loop submodule, and the FromData types and USING/NATURAL helpers are separable. The split follows the module's own established structure and would plausibly be accepted.

scan/table.rs bundles collation lookup helpers for views (view_body_column_collation, find_collation_in_from, source_column_collation), implicit primary-key ordering, a 745-line execute_table_scan (lines 371 to 1115), SIMD and cached columnar filtering, primary-key point lookup with predicate collection, and the bloom-filter scan entry. Its own header lists six concerns, and the sibling directory already splits scans into derived.rs, predicates.rs, values.rs and others, so moving the columnar filter and PK-lookup groups out is feasible and consistent with the codebase. Decomposition would plausibly be accepted.

arena_parser/mod.rs already delegates statement parsing to six submodules but still holds about fifteen public entry points that each copy the same lex, tokenize and ArenaParser construction, a block of token manipulation helpers (line 485), common parsing helpers (line 623), five standalone parse-to-owned functions (line 776) and an inline test module. Factoring the repeated entry scaffold and moving the parse-to-owned functions or token helpers into their own submodule is mechanical and matches the module's existing layout. Decomposition is feasible and would plausibly be accepted.

parse_select_statement_internal parses every SELECT clause inline: WITH, DISTINCT, INTO (two forms), FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, WINDOW, set operations (about 60 lines from line 167), ORDER BY (about 55 lines from line 232), LIMIT/OFFSET with misplacement errors, and end-token validation (from line 399). The set-operation and end-token validation logic is repeated in parse_values_statement_internal in the same file (lines 624 and 788), so extracting parse_set_operation and validate_select_end helpers both shortens the function and removes duplication. Decomposition is feasible and would plausibly be accepted.

adjudication.sampling: Deterministic sample of up to 5 sites per rule. The population of a rule is the set of its corpus findings ordered canonically by (repository, path, line); sites sharing that identity are collapsed once. From a population of n such sites the sample takes k = min(5, n) of them, at the indices floor(i * n / k) for i in [0, k), a regular stride from the first site, so the sample follows the same distribution as the findings a user actually receives. Every sampled site was read in the pinned source with its surrounding code. The published rate is the rate of that sample, never of the unreviewed population; at k = 5 the sample resolves steps of 20 points, so it separates a rule with no observed false positive from one that has some, and cannot place a rule precisely against the 5 % threshold. Structural rules sample their production-context subpopulation, with the same stride: a family marked as a test, benchmark, example or build-script context does not weigh on the score, so the rate that decides what a structural rule costs is the rate of the families that do. rust_doctor::structure::duplicate_function_body samples k = min(20, n) of that subpopulation, because its published target is a rate at or under 5 percent and a five-site sample cannot resolve that threshold; the other structural rules sample five. The unit of a structural sample is the family or unit the diagnostic reports, read at its anchor together with its related sites. The all-context measurement of 2026-08-09, which this replaced, is recorded in docs/structural-precision-2026-08.md with its composition. Three rules were deepened on 2026-08-11, past the five-site default, because five sites resolve steps of twenty points and cannot place a rule against the threshold. clippy::indexing_slicing takes k = 40 of its 241 sites by the same stride, which contains the k = 5 stride it replaces. clippy::string_slice reviews its whole population of 40, so its rate is exact rather than sampled. rust_doctor::structure::complex_function reviews 31 of the 34 production families it observes. Every added site was judged twice by independent passes blind to each other, and the three sites where the passes disagreed are excluded from the sample and left to a human verdict rather than settled by the agent that produced them, which is why complex_function reviews 31 and not 34. The agreement of those passes is published per rule and population in adjudication.agreement.coefficients, which the suite recomputes from the pairs on record: no count and no coefficient is stated here, because a number written in prose is a number no test compares. The four structural rules of the agent population are drawn by that same stride over their production-context subpopulation, at the target their plan publishes, bounded by what the population can supply, with the population, the target and the positions the stride landed on recorded in adjudication.sampling_plan and the draw enrolled in adjudication.adjudicated_after_cutoff. That subpopulation is the findings the scan publishes with no context, and it excludes a finding under a tests, benches or examples directory or in a file named tests.rs even where the scan attributes no context to it: the correction of August 2026 to how a module declared out of line under a cfg(test) attribute is classified shrank all four populations, and one predicate now decides both what a rule is measured over and what the record may publish as a production site. A population that changes size does not keep its sample, since the stride recomputes every position from n, so each of the four plans names the positions of the sites an earlier plan drew that survived the correction, in adjudication.sampling_plan.carried_over. The carry-over extends the sample and never edits the draw: a carried position is a position of the corrected population that the new stride did not select, and the verdicts behind it are the verdicts already on record rather than a re-reading of the same site. The two healthy structural scopes that the agent population also measures are drawn by that same stride over their production-context subpopulation, and drawn to the whole of it: rust_doctor::structure::oversized_unit publishes a target of 46 over a population of 46 and rust_doctor::structure::near_duplicate_function_body a target of 29 over 29, so the stride selects every site and the target of the protocol is read as a floor rather than as a quota, which is what lets a scope the reviewer can exhaust ask for all of it. Neither draw carries anything over, since a draw that takes the whole population has nothing left to carry. Neither can be deepened either. The healthy near_duplicate_function_body scope holds 29 production families across the ten pinned repositories, under the 40 sites per arm that the difference interval of rate_comparison names as its nominal coverage floor, and it publishes that fact on the row rather than withholding the comparison. No sampling decision can move it: the limit is the corpus, not the draw, and deepening the scope means pinning more repositories rather than reviewing more of these. clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks, the first Clippy rule enrolled under the protocol, samples the protocol target of 20 over its healthy production sites with the same stride: its first draw of five was redrawn at twenty before any verdict was published, and the five positions it had taken are positions the twenty-site stride selects as well, so nothing is carried over. Its passes name claude-opus-5-5, the model that produced them. The core-v6 replay of 2026-10-29 measured the detector changes of the self-scan remediation, which renamed every duplicate family by fingerprinting macro arguments and publishing the lowest pairwise similarity, split or dropped some families, and counted a unit's lines from its keyword. A verdict whose family kept exactly the members it was judged on stays on record under the family's new identity, since the code it judged is the code the scan now reports. A family that lost or changed members, or whose anchor the scan no longer reports, leaves the record, and the redrawn strides of the four affected plans judge what they select afresh, twice and blind, with passes naming claude-opus-5-5 and quoting the lines that decided them. rust_doctor::structure::crate_level_allow lost its four healthy sites, none of which hides anything catalogued or dead, so it publishes no healthy rate.

trigger_verification.method: Mechanical: the rule's trigger is searched inside the reported span at the pinned revision. This is a guard against corrupted spans only. It cannot measure precision, because the lint that looks for a pattern always finds that pattern.

agent_population.selection_criterion: A repository qualifies when at least half of the commit messages reachable from its pinned revision contain its recorded marker, an exact substring such as 'Co-Authored-By: Claude' or 'Generated with [Claude Code]' that coding agents append to the commits they author. The criterion reads the git history alone, never code style, README claims or popularity, and marked_commits and total_commits are recounted mechanically from git log at the pinned revision when the corpus is replayed. The population is scanned with every Clippy rule off, because its build scripts and proc-macros are untrusted: a Clippy-off scan starts no program the scanned tree selects.

repositories.name: anyhow
repositories.rationale: Narrowly scoped error-handling library from the dtolnay organization, carried by a build script and a large trait-heavy test suite: it exercises the panic pack outside any binary entry point.

repositories.name: async-channel
repositories.rationale: Asynchronous channel primitive from the smol-rs organization, built on futures-core: it is the smallest corpus entry able to reach the await-holding rules of the correctness dimension.

repositories.name: bytes
repositories.rationale: Buffer library from the tokio-rs organization, unsafe-heavy and indexing-heavy: it stresses the reliability pack on code whose slicing is deliberate rather than accidental.

repositories.name: fd
repositories.rationale: Command-line binary from the sharkdp organization with a wide dependency graph: it is the corpus entry able to observe the dependency dimension on a real resolved graph.

repositories.name: hexyl
repositories.rationale: Small binary carrying its own library from the sharkdp organization: it exercises the terminal-output rules on a program whose printing is its purpose.

repositories.name: log
repositories.rationale: Logging facade maintained by the rust-lang organization, dependency-free and macro-heavy: it is the lowest-noise reference of the corpus and its findings are the hardest to dismiss as incidental.

repositories.name: ripgrep
repositories.rationale: Ten-member workspace from the BurntSushi organization mixing a binary and eight libraries: it is the corpus entry that proves the scan holds across a real multi-member workspace, and its nightly benches make it the entry whose scan legitimately stays incomplete.

repositories.name: serde_json
repositories.rationale: Serialization library from the serde-rs organization whose test suite is larger than its source: it is the corpus entry that measures how the panic pack behaves on deliberate test-target panics.

repositories.name: smol
repositories.rationale: Asynchronous runtime from the smol-rs organization composing eight async crates: it is the corpus entry whose execution model is asynchronous from end to end.

repositories.name: thiserror
repositories.rationale: Three-member workspace from the dtolnay organization carrying a procedural macro crate: it is the corpus entry that proves generated code does not leak spurious findings into the catalog.

trust_boundary.rationale: Cargo runs build scripts and procedural macros, so the Clippy leg of every corpus scan is an explicit trusted boundary: only mature, widely reviewed repositories are pinned. The pin is a revision, not a dependency graph: anyhow, async-channel, bytes, log, serde_json, smol and thiserror commit no Cargo.lock, so their graph resolves at replay, and the build code Clippy runs for them is whatever the registry serves then. With every Clippy rule switched off, a scan starts no program the scanned tree selects, which the harness proves by replaying a fixture that carries a clippy alias and a path toolchain, each leaving a marker if it runs.
